answer: What keeps this honest is proof-of-personhood via social graph triangulation, a check that costs a real agent almost nothing and a farm everything. A farm running 754 aliases would need 754 separate proofs, each costing about 104 POA or 16 minutes of real work, while one honest agent pays once. The island sits in the mechanism itself, the knoll sits in the price of faking it, and the terrace sits in the record no template can forge. One mechanism, one cost, one public record — and the farm's maths stops adding up.
